title: Normalized unbounded derived open adjunction for condensed modules
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$. All schemes are separated of finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible [sk-def-localizing-closure], using [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. On a small representative of each small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $\mathcal C_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}(\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proet}},\Ab))$, where $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients; sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $h:V\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Use the specified module pullback and extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback; sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and the specified adjunction $h_!\dashv h^*$ [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction], with unit $u$ and counit $v$. Both functors are exact and additive, and the actual unit $u:1\to h^*h_!$ is invertible. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories $D(\mathcal C_T)$ with localization $Q_T$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $C(F)$ for termwise application of an additive functor and $a_{F,K}:D(F)QK\xrightarrow{\sim}QC(F)K$ for the canonical exact-functor factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. The specified termwise adjunction descends to $D(h_!)\dashv D(h^*)$ with unit $u_D$ and counit $v_D$ equal, under the $a_F$ comparisons, to $Q(C(u))$ and $Q(C(v))$. In particular, for every complex $K$ in $\mathcal C_V$,
$$a_{h^*,C(h_!)K}\circ D(h^*)(a_{h_!,K})\circ (u_D)_{Q_VK}=Q_V(C(u)_K).$$
The unit $u_D$ is invertible. With the canonical integer-shift identifications of these exact functors, $u_D$, $v_D$ and the derived adjunction Hom bijections commute with simultaneous shift of both variables by every integer. These assertions hold on all unbounded complexes without constructibility assumptions.

proof.text: The source library supplies additivity and preservation of finite limits and colimits for both actual module functors. Its module-object abelian and Grothendieck sheaf instances provide the abelian categories used by mapDerivedCategory. Assemble these instances directly; no resolution or constructibility argument is required.

The abelian open extension is fully faithful. The proved source-library Adjunction.fullyFaithfulMapModLeft lifts this full faithfulness through the projection-formula linearization. Restriction along the coefficient isomorphism is the equivalence Mod.comapEquivalenceOfIsIso. Compose these two fully faithful functors, which definitionally gives the specified module extension by zero. Mathlib Adjunction.unit_isIso_of_L_fully_faithful then makes the unit of the actual specified adjunction invertible.

Apply the existing Adjunction.mapHomologicalComplex to the specified adjunction. Supply CatCommSq structures using the inverses of the two canonical mapDerivedCategoryFactors isomorphisms. Adjunction.localization gives an adjunction on the full unbounded derived categories. Its localization_unit_app and localization_counit_app formulas give the two required normalizations, cancelling the inverse comparison maps for the displayed unit equation.

Each component of the cochain unit is an isomorphism because its degree i component is the original invertible unit. HomologicalComplex.Hom.isIso_of_components and functoriality of Q make its localized image invertible. The unit formula expresses every component over Q as a composite of three isomorphisms. Precomposition with Q is fully faithful, hence reflects isomorphisms, so the entire descended unit is invertible.

For each integer n, compute the cochain unit shift square in degree i: all shift comparison components are identities, leaving the same unit on K.X(i+n). Express whiskerLeft Q of the derived unit as the whiskered cochain unit followed by the inverse right and left factorization comparisons, with associators and unitors. Each factor commutes with integer shifts. The proved source lemma NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft transfers this property from Q to the whole derived category, using essential surjectivity of Q. Adjunction.CommShift.mk' gives the counit compatibility from the unit compatibility.

Write the Hom equivalence as unit followed by R of the given morphism. Postcompose both sides of the required equation with the invertible right shift comparison. Naturality of that comparison and the proved unit shift square identify the left side with the shift of the unit followed by the shift of R(f). Functorial preservation of composition proves the equality, for every integer n.
